Updated view incorporating SLOOS:
- FOMC tone: Moderately positive on growth and labor, balanced near-term risks, inflation running below 2%, policy still accommodative with gradual hikes expected and balance sheet normalization “relatively soon.”
- SLOOS cross-check: Domestic banks reported weaker demand for CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and consumer credit (auto, credit cards), with tighter standards for consumer loans. Mortgage-related standards generally eased (including jumbo, QM, and GSE), and home-purchase/HELOC standards were mostly unchanged. Foreign banks reported tighter standards across C&I (small, middle, large firms) and CRE, though CRE demand strengthened for foreign banks.
- Net effect: Credit conditions look mixed-to-slightly tighter, particularly for consumer and some business/CRE segments, which modestly tempers the otherwise neutral-to-positive FOMC tone.
